newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka army push halted by rebel resistance.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka army push halted by rebel resistance.

text.p: Sri Lankan forces halted a push into Tamil Tiger rebels' northern stronghold on Tuesday in the face of fierce guerrilla resistance, as Western aid workers reported the first civilian casualties in the fighting.

"The LTTE's resistance is very heavy," said a military officer at the Defence Ministry's Operational Headquarters. He was referring to the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, who seek an independent homeland for minority Tamils.
"We are consolidating our defences, and the offensive is not going on at the moment," he told Reuters.

The military, making its first major push against the guerrillas in more than a month, reported dominating an area near the town of Kilinochchi, the northern entry point to the Tigers' jungle territory of the Wanni.
But the military officer, who asked not to be named, said the troops, supported by air force bombers, artillery and tanks, were still several miles away from Kilinochchi.
Defence analysts said government troops tried to outflank the rebels, who were well dug in at Kilinochchi, 285 km (180 miles) north of Colombo.
A military spokesman said security forces killed 35 guerrillas and wounded 100 more in Monday's fighting, in which 15 soldiers were also killed and 21 wounded.
This brings the army's death toll to 37 and the number of wounded to 79 in the first two days of the renewed operation.
"Army casualties are pretty high. This means the LTTE is fighting back very strongly," an Asian diplomat said.
A spokeswoman for a Western aid team in the Wanni said a few civilians displaced by the fighting had arrived at an aid centre at Mallavi, southwest of Kilinochchi.
"A small number of people came in tractors and trailers," said Frances Stevenson of Medecins Sans Frontieres.
She told Reuters nine people with blast wounds were admitted to a medical facility at Akkarayan, about 15 km (nine miles) from Kilinochchi.
The army has said it wants to reopen the highway connecting Jaffna and Colombo, which passes through a large swathe of rebel-held territory separating Jaffna and the mainland.
An army major said the military suffered more casualties overnight in a guerrilla counter-attack on ground troops digging in south of the road junction town of Paranthan.
Paranthan is between Kilinochchi and the Elephant Pass at the neck of the northernmost Jaffna peninsula, which was recaptured by the army from the rebels in April.
The military spokesman said government troops either killed or wounded more than 200 rebels on Sunday.

The LTTE questioned the military claim. The LTTE's Voice of Tigers Radio said only 13 of its fighters were killed on Sunday and two more on Monday. "The Tigers are fighting fiercely against the forces," it said.
It was not possible to verify the conflicting claims as the government has banned journalists from visiting the war zone.
The military spokesman said air force Mi-24 helicopters and naval craft sank 10 rebel boats south of Vettilaikerni on the northeast coast in a separate clash, but Tiger casualties were not known.
The military balance has remained largely unchanged since the LTTE overran the northeastern Mullaitivu camp in July, killing or capturing almost its entire garrison of 1,400 men.
It was the military's worst setback in the 13-year war in which the government says more than 50,000 people have died.
